03What It IsOVERVIEW▶

A Claude skill for checking new rule proposals for the Fusion AI Rules before they join the set. A proposal can come from the Rule Set page's Propose on GitHub button, a file, pasted text, or someone's dashboard.

Claude files each proposal as a candidate, compares it with every active rule, writes up each conflict with fix options, and asks Swami once on a decision card. It then builds the accepted batch on a branch with the AI Rules Manager steps, ready for Swami to merge.

Why it mattersProposals often overlap or contradict rules that already work. Izzy's Symmetry and Mirror batch clashed with two existing rules; this skill turns that kind of review into a repeatable process with one clear decision.
04What It DoesOVERVIEW▶
  • CollectCopies each proposal verbatim into candidates/<batch>/ with a C- ID, the author's own label, and the next free R number as its proposed ID.
  • MapMarks each candidate as New, Tightens, Overlaps or Conflicts against every active rule, and records conflicts_with and related.
  • Conflict CardsWrites up each conflict with both texts quoted and 2 or 3 fix options, recommending the one that keeps Must rules intact and changes the least.
  • Fit CheckChecks priority, clarity, Fusion feature names as they appear in the UI, which AIs it works in, and length (about 600 characters or less).
  • Build CheckRuns python3 build/build.py check with the candidates in place, so IDs and references are valid.
  • DecisionAsks Swami once on a decision card, recommending "accept with the recommended fixes", and keeps working on that option meanwhile.
  • Result BranchBuilds the accepted batch with the AI Rules Manager steps and opens a pull request, unmerged until Swami decides and the author agrees to CC BY 4.0.
  • TestsMakes sure each accepted rule gets a test question in tests/prompts/, following the AI Rules Manager steps.
  • Review PageFor a large batch, or to share with the author, builds a Rule Review dashboard with the vibe-dashboard skill.

08Capabilities and LimitationsSCOPE▶
  • One DecisionBoils a batch down to a single decision card with a recommended option, so Swami answers once.
  • TraceableKeeps the author's original text, labels and a decisions table in sources/, so every accepted rule can be traced back.
  • Safe by DefaultThe build check runs with the candidates in place, and nothing merges without Swami.
  • Judgment CallsMapping and fix options are Claude's recommendations; Swami makes the decision.
  • No TestingIt doesn't test a candidate in each AI; new rules start as Untested until test runs are recorded.
  • Consent NeededAn outside author's rules can't merge until they agree to CC BY 4.0.
09Scheduled TasksRUNTIME▶

None. It runs when Swami asks for a rule change or a review. The repository's GitHub Action builds and publishes on every merge, but that is GitHub, not a Claude scheduled task.

11GotchasGOTCHAS▶
  • Verbatim FirstNever change the author's meaning while filing candidates; fixes come later, as recommendations.
  • Fiddly AreasCheck parameters and math (R08, R09), mirroring and timeline order, intersect or cut intent, and naming closely: that's where conflicts hide.
  • Major BumpsDeprecating or rewording an existing rule to fit a candidate is a major version bump.
  • Private DetailsNever put private links or names under NDA into anything that goes into the public repository.
12Other RequirementsREFERENCE▶
  • GitHub AccessSwami's GitHub connected to Claude, with the fusion-ai-rules repository attached with push access.
  • WindowsNothing extra: works the same from Windows 10 or 11.
